minutes.headline: Board put the farmers market under the agricultural commission and approved a MART commuter van starting April 13.
minutes.summary: The Select Board approved a one-day liquor license, moved the farmers market under the agricultural commission by policy and a bylaw article, and sent the cable renewal notice to Comcast. It backed mosquito control funding, approved a MART van schedule, and heard the town manager review governor's budget state aid for FY16. It ratified the animal inspector's appointment and discussed the tight warrant deadline.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to have the agricultural commission run this year's farmers market and to put bylaw language on the commission's charge on the town warrant.
The board voted to send a letter revoking the prior authority of the existing farmers market manager.
The board voted to go forward with the MART van schedule; the town will advertise service starting April 13, but the vote to start that date was not audible.
The board voted to send Comcast the notice that starts the cable license renewal, and voted to support the mosquito control budget.
The town manager reviewed FY16 state aid under the governor's budget, noting higher assessments and an uncertain one-time payment, and said the health insurance renewal came in higher.

why_it_matters: The farmers market's management is changing hands, and a bylaw change on the warrant means residents will be asked to vote on it at Town Meeting.
Higher state assessments reduce the net new state aid, and the one-time payment should not fund recurring costs, so the FY16 budget is tighter than the headline aid figures suggest.
A town-advertised MART commuter van is now planned, funded from available MBTA assessment money through the fiscal year.
watch_next: MART van service is planned to start April 13.
The sewer commission is to present a borrowing article for the Pleasantview sewer extension, repaid through betterments.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on most votes and on the budget figures both list, but ours leaves out much of what the official minutes record. The main differences are the animal inspector vote (the official gives 4-1 and names the appointee), the unheard MART start vote, the farmers market letter wording, and the Green Community Task Force outcome (standing committee in ours, tabled in the official).
